The instructions for this hydrogel mask are incredibly clear, making the application process completely straightforward. On clean-shaven skin, like my girlfriend's face, the mask fits flawlessly with absolutely zero gaps. It hugs the contours of the face perfectly. Just keep in mind that this is a deep-treatment mask. It took about 3 to 4 hours to completely dry down, turn translucent, and absorb fully into the skin. The main challenge comes if you have a trimmed beard or facial hair. The hydrogel material cannot grip hair, so the lower half of the mask will not stick properly and tends to fall off. Only the upper section secured well to my forehead and upper cheeks.However, we found some great creative workarounds so nothing went to waste! My girlfriend applied the remaining jaw and chin section to my neck 😂, which worked beautifully. We also used the tiny punch-out eye and mouth patches creatively, placing the extra pieces above my eyebrows and using the mouth cutout across the bridge of my nose for targeted hydration. Pros:Truly delivers a noticeable boost in skin hydration and plumpness. Leaves the skin feeling incredibly smooth, refreshed, and deeply nourished. High-quality ingredients that genuinely work, offering great value for money. Cons: Not beard-friendly, as the lower half slides off facial hair. Requires 3–4 hours to dry, so it is best used when you have plenty of time or as an overnight mask. Final Verdict:If you have a smooth, clean-shaven face, this mask is an easy 5-star product because the fit and skin benefits are flawless. If you have a beard, the lower half simply won't stick. However, because it is highly effective and versatile enough to be repurposed on your neck and nose, it still deserves a solid 4 stars. Highly recommended, but beard wearers beware! If the product/ cords/accessories are damaged, take it to an oral-b service centre. Do not modify or repair the product. This may cause fire, electric shock or injury. Usage by children under age 3 is not recommended. Toothbrushes can be used by children and persons with reduced physical, sensory or mental capabilities or lack of experience and knowledge, if they have been given supervision or instruction concerning use of the appliance in a safe way and understand the hazards involved. Cleaning and maintenance shall not be performed by children. Children shall not play with the appliance. Use this product only for its intended use as described in then instruction manual. Do not use attachments which are not recommended by the manufacturer. Directions: 1. Wet the toothbrush head and apply a pea-sized amount of toothpaste. 2. Place the toothbrush head against your teeth at a 45-degree angle to the gum line. 3. Press the power button to start the toothbrush and move it gently across all tooth surfaces in a circular motion. 4. Brush the outer, inner, and chewing surfaces of all teeth for about 2 minutes, ensuring you spend equal time on each section. 5. Brush your tongue and the roof of your mouth to remove bacteria and freshen your breath. 6. Rinse your mouth and the toothbrush thoroughly after brushing. 7. Replace the toothbrush head every 3 months or when the bristles become frayed. For the £23 I bought it for I'd say this is definitely not the worst investment I've ever made, and it absolutely does give me a far better tooth clean than any manual brush ever could. From that perspective it absolutely does what I bought it for. That being said though, I think I have to echo a lot of what other people have been saying about it, from the point of view of its downsides. I havent had quite the egregious battery life other people seem to have been experiencing, but I'd also hesitate to call the battery life "good". I live by myself, and I manage to get anywhere from two to three days out of it before it needs charging again. Its not absolutely terrible and I bought it knowing the battery life was a weak point, but if you have a full family thats using it then the battery won't last very long at all. This is a problem, considering that there's no way to know when the battery is getting low other than just how strong the motor feels when you're using it. Looking at the instructions, it seems like other models have an LED on them, but this one doesnt even have a single one. This both means that its hard to get an exact idea of when the battery needs charging, and also means you wont know when exactly its done charging either (I think maybe some people are experiencing poor battery life because they arent leaving it on for long enough, precisely because of that). You sort of just have to guess at when it might be done or check how strong the motor feels. Dont get me wrong, I like that its simple and I dont think its inherently a bad product - I intend to keep it an use it even with its flaws, just because it does everything I need it to, only really cost the equivalent of a few packets of toothburshes, and having the integrated timer is really useful. However I feel like they made it a little too simple for its own good. Not having even a single LED on there does kind of harm the functionality, given that the battery life isnt exactly stellar to begin with. I'm ok with that on balance since I'm the only one using it here, but it may well be worth it to most people to move slightly further up the like to a slightly higer end brush. I feel like its also worth noting, while we're on the subject, that the brush's charger only has a shaver plug connector, and it doesnt include an adapter for a standard wall socket. Thats fine if you have a shaver plug, but I feel like to an extent those are a dying breed so most people will also need a shaver plug adapter to use a normal socket with it, which is worth noting since it adds to the cost and it isnt really mentioned on the product page (albeit not especially significantly). It comes with two brush heads, which are very easy to swap over, making it convenient if more than one person wants to use the handle or when replacing heads. The toothbrush also offers three cleaning modes/speed settings, which is a nice feature at this price point and allows you to choose a setting that feels most comfortable. There’s a 2-minute total brushing reminder, along with 30-second interval alerts to encourage you to move between different areas of your mouth for more even brushing. The handle itself is lightweight, comfortable to hold, and straightforward to operate with a single button. The main downside is the battery life. There’s no proper charging light or battery status indicator, so it’s difficult to tell whether it’s charging correctly or when it has fully charged. Overall, it’s a decent entry-level electric toothbrush with useful features and good cleaning performance, but the battery and charging setup definitely falls behind more modern alternatives. " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Cost-Per-Hour Test Results & Unboxing Video Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. Top reviews from the United Kingdom Jade 5 out of 5 stars The honest truth that hasn't been spoon fed to me by Tiktok Influencers Reviewed in the United Kingdom on 9 July 2026 Verified Purchase Brief content visible, double tap to read full content. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. You've seen this on Tiktok, that's why you're here, probably trying to ensure you buy a genuine Medicube product rather than risking a fake. Good call. I also saw this on Tiktok, and was baffled by the blatant lies and exaggerations, which I believe is the reason this product has 4 stars. Tiktok calls it.. well I won't say what Tiktok calls it in case it gets my review declined, but let's just say they compare it to filler. If you're buying this product because you believe it's got the same ingredients as implants(?), it's so powerful that if you put it on your finger it'll swell up like a balloon, or you will see instant results, then please believe me when I tell you that firstly - you are Tiktok's ideal demographic, and secondly - you're gonna be disappointed in this product. If you're buying it because you've read about volufiline, but maybe don't want to jump straight to stronger forms of it, like the Ordinary serum for example, and you're willing to give the skincare a chance to actually work, you might just love this product. It is not 'vaseline in a stick', nor is it some miracle product that's gonna immediately rid you of your eye bags and crows feet. It is a dose of hydration around areas that need a little more attention as we age, and the ingredients do have some scientific backing behind them - with the caveat that the effects are subtle and are not a replacement for filler. Volufiline stimulates fat cells, causing the plumping effect that's so grossly misrepresented on Tiktok. I've been using for about a week every day, and I am noticing subtle differences in my under eye area, the shadows are lessening, and the delicate skin feels hydrated. Skincare girlies (and guys) know that skincare products need 6 weeks to be tested properly, so I'm excited that I can visibly see improvements in such a short period. I like the application, the product being in stick form means I can easily apply it quickly without worrying about wasted product, which can be an issue with the Ordinary serum - although the comparison isn't fair as the products are completely different in strength. The product is very gentle, and I have eczema, sporadic psoriasis and sensitive skin in general, this has caused no redness, irritation or stinging. Value wise, the price is likely up due to the product going viral, but I was pleased with the results so in my opinion the product is worth it, I would also advise (but you know, who am I to tell you what to do?) to buy the genuine Medicube balm, rather than the crop of 'dupes' that have sprung up trying to cash in on the hype. You and your skin, particularly your eyes, deserve quality ingredients, not a mish mash of cheap imitations smushed together and marketed as a dupe. As I haven't tested the product for long enough to make a fair assessment on the long term effects, what I will say is that at worst, it's a convenient, quality dose of hydration for areas that need it most, and at it's best I can see improvements in glow, skin quality and volume in the areas of my face that need a little top up. Remember - if something seems too good to be true, it usually is. I like the product, I like Medicube in general as a brand, and I would recommend this product based on what I've seen so far. I have been using the Shark FlexStyle Multistyler for several weeks now, and I can honestly say it has completely changed my hair styling routine. The first thing that impressed me was how lightweight and easy it is to use. I have fairly long hair, and traditional hair dryers and styling tools often leave my arms tired by the time I'm finished. The Shark FlexStyle feels comfortable to hold and the rotating design makes it incredibly versatile. The Auto-Wrap Curlers were the feature I was most excited about, and they did not disappoint. I was a little skeptical at first because I've struggled with curling my own hair using conventional curling wands. However, the FlexStyle automatically wraps sections of hair around the barrel using airflow, making the process surprisingly simple. After a few attempts, I was able to create beautiful, bouncy curls that looked like I had just come from a salon. The curls lasted most of the day, especially when I used a light styling spray. The Oval Brush attachment is another standout feature. It gives my hair a smooth, voluminous blowout look without needing to juggle a separate brush and hair dryer. My hair tends to become frizzy, particularly in humid weather, but this attachment helped create a sleek finish with noticeable volume at the roots. I also appreciated the Concentrator attachment for everyday drying. It directs airflow precisely where it's needed and helps achieve a polished look much faster than my previous hair dryer. The difference is noticeable straight away. My teeth feel much cleaner after brushing, and the iO2 is surprisingly quiet compared with other electric toothbrushes I’ve used. I really like having the pressure sensor because it’s easy to accidentally brush too hard, and the different intensity settings mean I can adjust it depending on how my teeth and gums feel. The handles are comfortable to hold and the battery life has been good, so I’m not constantly having to charge them. Getting two handles, two brush heads and the travel cases makes this feel like a much better deal than buying a single toothbrush. The black and forest green colours also look much better than the usual plain toothbrushes. The only thing I’d mention is to rinse the brush and handle properly after use, as toothpaste can build up around the head and smaller areas. Overall, I’m very happy with the purchase. Yes Product description Product Description HG Mould Spray is a fast-acting black mould remover for walls and household surfaces affected by visible mould, mildew, fungus and algae in damp areas. Its targeted, self-acting spray has a bleaching action and works in around 30 minutes, helping remove stains without scrubbing on compatible surfaces. Use it indoors in bathrooms, showers, toilets, kitchens, cellars, basements and saunas on suitable plastered walls, tiles, grout, silicone joints, window frames and other compatible surfaces. It can also be used outdoors around compatible swimming pools, facades, balconies, plant boxes and garden ornaments, excluding wood. One 500ml bottle treats approximately 2–3 m² of wall surface or 6–8 m² of tile grout. Ensure good ventilation and wear suitable rubber or plastic gloves. Remove the safety clip or unlock the nozzle. Spray from approximately 3–5cm away and leave for 30 minutes. Clean the treated area with water and a sponge. For stubborn stains, reapply and leave for a further 30 minutes. For silicone joints, wash off after 30 minutes and repeat if necessary. Always test first in an inconspicuous area. Permanent brown discolouration may occur on elastic grouting, badly glazed tiles or old tiles with hairline cracks. Do not use on wood, coloured surfaces, ceilings, clothing, paintwork, plastic shower trays, vertical blinds, aluminium, stainless steel or other sensitive metals. Avoid splashes and do not reuse the bottle. Never mix with other cleaning products, as dangerous chlorine gas may be released. Wash hands after handling. Store and transport cool, dark and upright. Very toxic to aquatic life; avoid release into the environment. Keep out of reach of children and read the label before use. I’ve used this spray on silicone sealant that I thought would require expensive replacement due to dark black mould spots. To my surprise, just a couple of applications completely eradicated the mould! For very deep, dark, or large areas of mould that have penetrated the sealant, multiple applications may be necessary, but even then, the mould fades significantly. This product works wonders not just on bathroom and kitchen sealants but also on discoloured grout, window frames and seals, skirting boards, backs of furniture (with care—always test a small area first and avoid soaking expensive or varnished items), and bathroom/shower walls and ceilings. The spray does have a strong chemical odour similar to bleach, so proper precautions are essential. I recommend wearing a mask and goggles (especially if spraying higher areas like ceilings) and ensuring the room is well-ventilated by opening windows. With common-sense safety measures in place, it’s easy to use effectively. As someone who works in property management and deals with over 20 properties annually that have condensation-related mould issues, this product has been a lifesaver. It allows me to resolve mould problems quickly and efficiently. We also use it routinely between tenancies to clean bathrooms—grout, sealant, and ceilings—saving significant time compared to scrubbing grout with bleach or replacing sealant altogether. In my own home, I used to replace the shower sealant every 12–18 months due to mould buildup. Since using this spray, the sealant looks like new and stays fresh for years! Regularly spraying as soon as mould spots appear prevents the need for multiple applications and makes one bottle last an impressively long time. I’ve only deducted one star for minor reasons: the product takes several hours to work its magic (so patience is required), multiple applications may be needed for severe mould cases, and the odour can be quite strong when working with large areas. The internal tube now needs inserting before first use—it’s slightly inconvenient but helps prevent damage from long-term chemical exposure if stored unused for extended periods. Overall, this product is nothing short of amazing. It’s transformed how I deal with mould at home and in my work. If you’re looking for an effective solution to tackle stubborn mould problems without breaking the bank or spending hours scrubbing, I highly recommend giving this a try!
